value.body: A corporate lawyer works at a law firm advising companies on deals and business matters. Clients include companies, investors and founders. A typical day involves drafting and reviewing transaction documents, running due diligence on companies, researching regulations, and working to deadlines set by deals.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: LLB (3-year after graduation, or 5-year integrated after Class 12)

items.label: Common work
items.value: Mergers and acquisitions, fundraising, joint ventures, securities and regulatory advice

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Word processors, virtual data rooms, legal research databases

items.label: Enrolled advocates
items.note: On State Bar Council rolls; includes inactive members still listed. Corporate lawyers are a small share
items.source: Ministry of Law and Justice, Rajya Sabha reply (as reported)

items.label: LL.B. students (regular mode)
items.note: 3-year LL.B. only; integrated 5-year degrees are counted separately

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Firms usually hire freshers as associates, often from law school campus placements or after internships at the firm. Good academic records and drafting skills matter. Enrolling with a State Bar Council is common but is not always needed for advisory (non-court) work.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Drafting share purchase, investment and shareholder agreements
Due diligence on companies and their records
Legal research on company, securities and foreign investment law
Working in teams under tight deal deadlines

value.title: At a glance
items: Common path: associate → senior associate → principal associate → partner.
Hours can be long, especially near deal closings.
Experience here often leads to in-house legal roles later.
Hiring is concentrated in large cities.

value.title: LL.B. enrolment, regular mode
value.note: Regular mode only; 3-year LL.B. programme. Based on institutions that responded to the survey; part of the year-to-year change reflects response coverage.
